## What this dispatch delivers, and nothing more

M12 — accepted deterministic state-effect agreement — end to end: the canonical
runtime event, its durable admission, the measurement, and the machine-
comparable fixture expectation it is measured against. It does NOT inject a
packet, does NOT render a packet, and does NOT create the intervention seam.
Those are dispatches 1 and 3. Do not create
`packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts`; another agent owns that file on
a parallel branch.

## Why M12 does not exist yet

Design §13.1 defines **M12** as *accepted state-effect agreement* — "whether the
accepted deterministic state effect matches the fixture's expectation
(including the expectation that there is none)". §13.3 admits M1–M11 at Phase 2
and M1–M12 from Phase 3, and Erratum 1 (§9.6) confirms M12, not M11, is the
deterministic-agreement measurement B3 gates. W9 shipped M1–M11. M12 is
missing, and it is the measurement that separates Phase 3 from Phase 2.

Two things block it today:

1. **No canonical accepted-state-effect event.** `turn_trace.accepted_state_delta`
   (`packages/core/src/orchestrator/turnTraceProjection.ts:138-153`) records the
   mutating calls' ARGS but drops the tool name for every tool except
   `spend_spell_slot`, and carries no attempt number. An anonymous args blob
   cannot be compared with an expectation.
2. **The fixture expectation is prose.** `DeterministicStateEffect` in
   `packages/core/test/diagnostics/fixtureContract.ts` carries only `statement`
   and `evidence`. Prose is not comparable. Design amendment 11.1 already set
   the precedent for this exact defect class: field 9 held material M9 could
   not measure, and the fix was to narrow the CONTRACT, not to add
   classification logic inside the measurement.

## Deliverable 1 — one predicate, one owner

`turnTraceProjection.ts` decides what counts as an accepted state mutation
(`call.mutates && call.result.ok`, with `spend_spell_slot` excluded unless its
result reports `spent === true`). M12 must apply the SAME rule. Do not copy it.

Extract it into an exported `isAcceptedStateMutation(call: ExecutedToolCall):
boolean` in `packages/core/src/orchestrator/turnTraceProjection.ts`, make
`deriveTraceFields` call it, and have the new recording path call it too. Two
copies of this rule are two things that can drift, and a drift means M12 and the
turn trace would describe the same turn differently.

## Deliverable 2 — the canonical event

In `packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts`, beside `RuntimeCapabilityInvocation`:

```ts
export interface RuntimeStateEffect {
  /** Primary-DM candidate attempt this effect was accepted on, counting from 1. */
  readonly attempt: number;
  /** Position in the accepted candidate's executed tool stream, from 0. */
  readonly ordinal: number;
  readonly tool: string;
  /** The tool's arguments, as executed. */
  readonly args: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}
```

Write the doc comment in the register the file already uses: say why every
field is required, why this is an event recorded at the ACCEPT boundary and not
a reconstruction from `accepted_state_delta`, and that a rejected attempt's
mutations roll back and therefore produce no event here.

In `shadow.ts`, beside `runtimeCapabilityInvocation`, add the projection:

```ts
export interface ObservedStateMutation {
  readonly tool: string;
  readonly args?: unknown;
}
export function acceptedStateEffects(
  calls: readonly ObservedStateMutation[],
  attempt: number,
): readonly RuntimeStateEffect[];
```

taking the ALREADY-FILTERED accepted mutations in execution order. Discovery
owns the durable shape and therefore owns this projection; the orchestrator
applies `isAcceptedStateMutation` and hands the survivors in, importing nothing
from discovery beyond `shadow.js` and `types.js`
(`packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryBoundary.test.ts` pins that seam — do
not widen it). A non-object `args` is normalized to `{}` at the projection, not
asserted through.

## Deliverable 3 — record it at the accept boundary

In `orchestrator.ts`, record the accepted candidate's state effects at BOTH
acceptance sites — the no-auditor break path and the audited accept path —
carrying the attempt number that was actually running. Record nothing on a
rejected attempt. Gate it on the existing `deps.recordDiscoveryShadow === true`
flag exactly as the capability observations are gated; do not add a second
flag.

Extend `RuntimeDiscoveryObservations` in `measurements.ts` with a required
`stateEffects: readonly RuntimeStateEffect[]` and thread it through
`completeDiscoveryShadowEvidence`. Required, not optional: an optional field
would make "the turn produced no accepted mutation" and "nobody recorded
anything" the same value, which is the green-looking nothing §13.3 forbids —
the empty array is a real observation, an absent field is not.

## Deliverable 4 — schema v2

Adding a required field to the durable evidence invalidates v1 rows, and the
reader is fail-closed by design. Bump `DISCOVERY_SHADOW_SCHEMA` to
`discovery-shadow-v2`, rename `assertV1` accordingly, and extend it to admit
`runtime.stateEffects`: an array; each entry an object with a finite non-
negative integer `attempt`, a finite non-negative integer `ordinal`, a
non-empty string `tool`, and an object `args`. Reject a malformed entry with
`DiscoveryShadowSchemaError` exactly as the existing checks do. Keep the
validator's declared-here-not-imported discipline: state the contract
independently of the producer.

Do NOT write a v1 migration and do NOT accept v1 rows. This is an experiment's
observational schema with no released consumers; a reader that silently admits
an older row would be admitting evidence that cannot answer M12.

Note for the reviewer's benefit, in your completion notes: dispatch 3 will
extend v2 further with the injection-delivery record. v2 is the one bump; do not
reserve, stub, or half-declare anything for it here.

## Deliverable 5 — the measurement

In `measurements.ts`, add the expectation input and the measurement. Keep
`measureRuntimeDiscovery`'s existing signature and behaviour unchanged (W9's
tests depend on it); M12 is a separate exported function, because its input is a
fixture expectation and M10/M11's is not.

```ts
export interface ExpectedStateEffectOperation {
  readonly tool: string;
  /** Argument fields that must match exactly on the paired accepted call.
   *  A subset: fields absent here are not compared. */
  readonly args?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}
export type ExpectedStateEffect =
  | { readonly expectation: 'none' }
  | {
      readonly expectation: 'effect';
      readonly operations: readonly ExpectedStateEffectOperation[];
    };

export interface StateEffectMeasurement {
  readonly expectation: 'none' | 'effect';
  readonly expectedOperations: readonly ExpectedStateEffectOperation[];
  readonly acceptedEffects: readonly RuntimeStateEffect[];
  readonly agreement: 'agreed' | 'disagreed';
  readonly disagreements: readonly StateEffectDisagreement[];
}

export function measureAcceptedStateEffect(
  runtime: RuntimeDiscoveryObservations,
  expected: ExpectedStateEffect,
): StateEffectMeasurement;
```

Semantics, stated exactly:

- `expectation: 'none'` agrees when `runtime.stateEffects` is empty, and
  disagrees otherwise with one `unexpected-effect` disagreement per recorded
  effect, each naming its tool, attempt and ordinal.
- `expectation: 'effect'` pairs each expected operation, IN DECLARED ORDER,
  against the accepted effects in ordinal order: the first not-yet-consumed
  accepted effect whose `tool` matches. An expected operation with no match is
  a `missing-expected-operation` disagreement. A matched operation whose
  declared `args` subset does not deep-equal the corresponding fields of the
  accepted call's `args` is an `argument-mismatch` disagreement naming the
  field, the expected value and the observed value. Accepted effects left
  unconsumed are `unexpected-effect` disagreements.
- `agreement` is `'agreed'` exactly when `disagreements` is empty. There is no
  third value and no "not comparable": unlike M10, both sides of this
  comparison are always present — the fixture always declares an expectation
  and the accepted attempt always produced a (possibly empty) recorded set.
  Declare that reasoning in the doc comment so a later revision does not add a
  soft state.
- M12 is NOT aggregated, scored, or reported as a rate. Say so in the doc
  comment, citing §13.2.

Export the new types and function from `packages/core/src/internal.ts` beside
the existing measurement exports. Nothing goes into the root
`packages/core/src/index.ts`.

## Deliverable 6 — fixture contract Amendment D

```ts
export interface DeterministicStateEffect {
  readonly kind: 'effect';
  readonly statement: string;
  readonly evidence: string;
  /** The accepted mutating tool operations this effect consists of, in order. */
  readonly operations: readonly ExpectedStateEffectOperation[];
}
```

with `ExpectedStateEffectOperation` declared test-locally in
`fixtureContract.ts` (the contract file cannot import from `src/`; the existing
`RouteClass` duplication and the `Exact<>` guard in
`packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryBoundary.test.ts` are the precedent —
add the same compile-time agreement assertion there for the new shape so the
two declarations cannot drift).

Validate it in the fixture validator: `operations` present and non-empty
whenever `kind` is `'effect'`, each entry an object with a non-empty string
`tool` and an optional plain-object `args`, with exact-key checking like every
other shape in that file. `ExplicitNone` continues to mean `expectation: 'none'`
— no operations, no new field.

Fill in P8's `operations` with the operation the fixture already names in its
own `expectedCapabilityStatus.inputs`:
`{ tool: 'use_item', args: { instanceId: 'ammunition-stack-1', operationId: 'hit-target' } }`.
Verify those two values against `p08Ammunition.ts`'s `campaignState` and against
how `packages/core/test/discovery/shadowRuntime.test.ts` actually calls
`use_item` for P8 before you write them; if they disagree, the fixture's own
declared state wins and you record the discrepancy in your notes. No other probe
changes: all eleven others declare `none` and stay as they are.

Record the amendment in the design document as a new subsection **§11.2 —
Amendment D: the expected deterministic state effect is machine-comparable**,
in `docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`,
immediately after §11.1. Follow §11.1's exact form: date (2026-09-10), owning
bead (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`), status line stating what it narrows and what it does
not change, the defect, and the change. State plainly that it changes no
measurement DEFINITION — §13.1's M12 is unchanged — and only makes the fixture
side of that comparison expressible. This is the only design-document edit in
this dispatch.

## Evidence required

Extend the existing suites rather than adding a parallel one where an existing
file already owns the surface.

E1. `packages/core/test/discovery/shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts` — accepted
    state effects are recorded from a REAL turn through the real registry and
    re-read out of SQLite: a turn whose accepted candidate calls a mutating
    tool records one event with the right tool, attempt and ordinal; a turn
    that calls only non-mutating tools records an empty array, not an absent
    field.
E2. The rejected-attempt case, mirroring the existing
    "capability events survive an audit-rejected attempt" block: an attempt
    whose mutations were ROLLED BACK contributes NO state effect, and the
    accepted attempt's effects carry the accepted attempt's number. This is the
    load-bearing case — it is the difference between "what the turn accepted"
    and "what the turn tried".
E3. `spend_spell_slot` with `spent: false` produces no event, and with
    `spent: true` produces one — through `isAcceptedStateMutation`, proving the
    one predicate governs both the turn trace and M12.
E4. `packages/core/test/discovery/shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts` — the v2
    reader ADMITS a well-formed row and REJECTS each malformed
    `runtime.stateEffects` shape (not an array; entry not an object; missing or
    non-string `tool`; missing, negative or non-integer `attempt`; missing or
    non-integer `ordinal`; non-object `args`). Also assert a v1 schema tag is
    rejected with the schema error.
E5. A new `packages/core/test/discovery/stateEffectMeasurement.test.ts` for
    `measureAcceptedStateEffect`: `none` agreeing on an empty set; `none`
    disagreeing and naming every unexpected effect; `effect` agreeing on an
    exact match; ordered pairing with an interleaved unrelated mutation;
    `missing-expected-operation`; `argument-mismatch` naming field, expected and
    observed; an unconsumed accepted effect reported as unexpected; and the
    subset rule (an argument field the expectation does not declare never
    causes a mismatch).
E6. P8's M12 measured over a real turn: drive the P8 scenario with a scripted
    model that calls `use_item`, and assert `measureAcceptedStateEffect` against
    the fixture's own `operations` reports `agreed`. Put it wherever P8's
    runtime turn already lives (`shadowRuntime.test.ts`) rather than rebuilding
    that setup.
E7. The fixture-contract validator rejects an `effect` with no `operations`,
    with an empty `operations`, with a non-string `tool`, and with an unknown
    key — beside the existing contract-validation tests.
